brief.headline: Push for a 2–3% price cut against faster payment: they earn 5.9% net margin vs 3.8% peer median and carry a 12.19% borrowing cost we can relieve.

priceAsk.summary: Request a 2–3% reduction in unit price for rigid plastic packaging in exchange for payment acceleration.
priceAsk.target: A discount reflecting their 12.19% effective borrowing rate — paying 15 days faster frees ₹22.57 L of our working capital and is worth ~1.67% annualised to them; use that to anchor a 2–3% price cut.
priceAsk.basis: They run a 5.9% net margin, 210 basis points above the 3.8% peer median. The gap shows pricing headroom. Their 104d cash-conversion cycle vs 79d peer median means they value faster cash; offering early payment gives us leverage to extract the saving.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to move from 30 Days After Receipt to 15 Days After Receipt in return for the price concession.

brief.financialLeverage: Chemco's 5.9% net margin beats the peer median of 3.8%, and their 16.3% return on capital exceeds the 14.9% peer median — they are profitable and efficient. CRISIL A+ / Stable rating and 2.94x interest coverage mean low financial distress, so we can negotiate firmly. However, their Altman Z-score of 2.17 sits in the grey zone, signalling modest stress; avoid an overly aggressive squeeze that could destabilise a supplier on the cusp. Our ₹5.49 Cr spend is only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue, so we have limited volume leverage — lead with the payment-speed trade, not threats. Their 12.19% borrowing cost and 104d cash cycle vs 79d peer median mean early payment is genuinely valuable to them.

evidence.point: Chemco's net margin is 210 basis points above the peer median, indicating room to cut price.
They tie up cash 25 days longer than peers, so faster payment from us has real value.
Their effective borrowing cost is double-digit, making early payment worth that rate to them.
Paying them 15 days earlier frees significant working capital for us.
They already stretch their own suppliers 12 days beyond the peer median, so asking for faster terms from them is fair reciprocity.
Our spend is a tiny slice of their revenue, limiting our volume leverage.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, with pharma bottles, caps, and preforms capability — a direct, credible second source with B (65/100) health.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, A (79/100) health) specialising in pails, containers, and pharma packaging — financially robust and operationally proven.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging supplier (₹701.17 Cr revenue) with broad bottle/cap capability, though C (57/100) health warrants closer due diligence.

risks: Altman Z-score of 2.17 places them in the grey zone — pushing too hard on price could tip a modestly stressed supplier into real distress and jeopardise continuity.
Our ₹5.49 Cr (0.59% of their revenue) gives us minimal volume clout; threatening to walk may not be credible without a qualified alternate already onboarded.
They already pay suppliers slowly (49d vs 37d peer median) and run a long 104d cash cycle — if we extend terms further without offsetting with faster payment, we risk straining their liquidity.

HDPE resin import benchmark is 87.61 ₹/kg, but we lack our own average or best price data for rigid plastic packaging, so we cannot cite a specific rupee gap to anchor the ask — rely instead on margin and borrowing-cost logic.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to explore moving to 15-day payment in exchange for a 2–3% price reduction — it accelerates cash for you at your 12.19% borrowing cost, and narrows the gap between your 5.9% margin and the 3.8% peer median we see across the category.
